youtube.description:
How does a petrol pump nozzle stop automatically? No sensor, no chip, no electricity. Inside the nozzle, petrol rushes through a narrow spot, speeds up and creates suction. That suction pulls air in through a thin tube that ends at a small air hole near the tip of the spout. While the hole is in open air, it just sips air and the petrol keeps flowing. When the tank fills and petrol covers the hole, air can't get in, the suction jumps, and it tugs a rubber diaphragm in the handle that trips the valve shut. That's the click. So how does a gas pump know when the tank is full? It doesn't: it feels its little straw get blocked.
